title: The Slow Traveler
author: a travel memoir
desc: 一位拒絕搭飛機的作家，坐夜車橫越歐亞，用在地美食認識每一座城市。

intro: I'm reading a travel memoir called 'The Slow Traveler.' The author refuses to fly and crosses continents by rail!
我在讀一本叫《慢旅人》的旅行回憶錄。作者拒絕搭飛機，用鐵路橫越大陸！

q: She argues that flying 'erases the distance' and robs you of the journey. Do you agree that how you travel matters as much as where you go?
她主張搭飛機「抹去了距離」，奪走了旅程本身。你同意怎麼旅行和去哪裡一樣重要嗎？
o: Completely. The journey is half the experience.
完全同意。旅程本身就佔了一半的體驗。
completely = 完全地。
She'd love you. She spends whole chapters just watching the landscape shift.
她會很喜歡你。她用整整幾章只在看風景變化。
In theory, but my vacation days are limited.
理論上同意，但我的假期有限。
in theory = 理論上。limited = 有限的。
That's the privilege problem, and she acknowledges it candidly.
這就是特權的問題，她也坦率地承認了。
Not really. I just want to arrive and explore.
不太同意。我只想抵達然後探索。
Not really = 不太，委婉的不同意。
A fair position. For many people, the destination is the whole point.
合理的立場。對很多人來說，目的地就是全部重點。

q: On the overnight train from Vienna to Venice, she shares a sleeper compartment with strangers. Would you be comfortable with that?
在從維也納到威尼斯的夜車上，她和陌生人共用一間臥鋪車廂。你會自在嗎？
o: Sure, it's a chance to meet interesting people.
當然，這是認識有趣的人的機會。
a chance to = 一個…的機會。
That's her favorite part. The best stories come from the people in the next bunk.
那是她最喜歡的部分。最好的故事都來自隔壁鋪位的人。
I'd pay extra for a private cabin.
我會多付錢訂私人包廂。
pay extra = 額外付費。cabin = 包廂、艙房。
Totally reasonable. A good night's sleep is worth the upgrade.
完全合理。一夜好眠值得升級。
Only with earplugs and an eye mask.
只要有耳塞和眼罩就可以。
earplugs = 耳塞。eye mask = 眼罩。
The seasoned traveler's survival kit!
資深旅人的生存工具包！

q: She misses a connection in Belgrade and ends up with a nine-hour layover. How do you usually handle unexpected delays?
她在貝爾格勒錯過轉乘，最後要等九個小時。你通常怎麼面對意料之外的延誤？
o: I explore the area around the station.
我會去車站附近探索。
area around = 周邊地區。
Exactly what she does. That layover becomes one of the book's best chapters.
她正是這麼做的。那次轉乘等待成了書中最棒的章節之一。
I get frustrated, I'll admit.
我承認我會很煩躁。
I'll admit = 我承認。frustrated = 挫折、煩躁的。
Completely human. Even she has a meltdown at the ticket office.
很有人性。連她都在售票處崩潰過。
I find a café and catch up on reading.
我會找間咖啡廳補看書。
catch up on = 補做（落後的事）。
A reader's best strategy. Delays are just bonus reading time!
讀者最好的策略。延誤就是額外的閱讀時間！

q: Her central argument is that slow travel shrinks our carbon footprint. Would environmental concerns ever change how you travel?
她的核心論點是：慢旅行能縮小碳足跡。環保考量會改變你的旅行方式嗎？
o: They already have. I take trains when I can.
已經改變了。能搭火車我就搭。
They already have (changed). 省略重複的動詞。
Every shift counts. Europe's night-train revival suggests it's working.
每個改變都有意義。歐洲夜車的復興顯示這是有效的。
I'd like to, but trains are often pricier.
我想，但火車常常比較貴。
pricier = 更貴的（口語）。
A real barrier. She argues for better subsidies in the final chapter.
確實是個障礙。她在最後一章主張要有更好的補貼。
Probably not. Convenience wins for me.
大概不會。對我來說便利最重要。
A wins = A 勝出。
An honest answer, and honesty is where real change starts.
誠實的回答，而誠實正是真正改變的起點。

end: All aboard for the next chapter! Next time, let's talk about food on the road.
下一章要發車了！下次來聊旅途中的美食。

intro: The second half of 'The Slow Traveler' is basically a love letter to local food.
《慢旅人》的後半部基本上是一封寫給在地美食的情書。

q: She has one rule: never eat anywhere with a menu in five languages. Is that a smart rule or a bit snobbish?
她有一條規則：絕不在菜單有五種語言的地方吃飯。這是聰明的規則，還是有點勢利？
o: Smart. Tourist traps are real.
聰明。觀光客陷阱真的存在。
tourist trap = 觀光客陷阱（貴又不道地的店）。
Very true. The prices double and the authenticity halves.
真的。價格加倍，道地程度減半。
A bit snobbish. Some great places welcome tourists.
有點勢利。有些很棒的店也歡迎觀光客。
a bit = 有點。welcome 當動詞 = 歡迎。
Fair point. Plenty of family restaurants translate their menus out of kindness.
說得好。很多家庭餐館翻譯菜單是出於好意。
It's a good rule of thumb, not an absolute law.
這是個不錯的經驗法則，不是絕對定律。
rule of thumb = 經驗法則。absolute = 絕對的。
A nuanced take. She actually breaks it herself in Lisbon.
很有層次的看法。她自己在里斯本就破例了。

q: In Istanbul, she eats grilled fish sandwiches straight off the boats. What street food would you recommend to a visitor in your city?
在伊斯坦堡，她直接在船邊吃烤魚三明治。你會推薦來你城市的旅客吃什麼街頭小吃？
o: Braised pork rice. It's simple but iconic.
滷肉飯。簡單卻具代表性。
braised = 燉滷的。iconic = 具代表性的。
I'm sure that's on her list for the next book!
我很確定那會在她下一本書的清單上！
Oyster omelets at the night market.
夜市的蚵仔煎。
oyster = 牡蠣、蚵仔。omelet = 煎蛋餅。
The texture sounds fascinating: crispy, chewy, and savory all at once.
口感聽起來很迷人：酥脆、Q彈、鹹香一次到位。
Scallion pancakes, fresh off the griddle.
剛從鐵板上起鍋的蔥油餅。
scallion = 青蔥。fresh off = 剛從…出來。griddle = 鐵板煎鍋。
'Fresh off the griddle' is the key phrase. Street food is all about timing!
「剛起鍋」是關鍵。街頭小吃重點就在時機！

q: In Oaxaca, she takes a cooking class and learns to grind chocolate by hand for mole sauce. Would you rather take a cooking class or join a food tour?
在瓦哈卡，她上了烹飪課，學會手工研磨巧克力做莫雷醬。你寧願上烹飪課，還是參加美食導覽？
o: A cooking class. I want to bring the skill home.
烹飪課。我想把技能帶回家。
bring ... home = 把…帶回家。
That's her reasoning too: a recipe is a souvenir that never gathers dust.
她也是這麼想：食譜是永遠不會積灰塵的紀念品。
A food tour. More variety in less time.
美食導覽。花更少時間吃到更多樣。
more ... in less time = 用更少時間得到更多。
Efficient! A good guide also tells you the stories behind each dish.
很有效率！好的導遊還會告訴你每道菜背後的故事。
Both, ideally on the same day.
兩個都要，最好在同一天。
ideally = 理想情況下。
Ambitious! Just remember to pace your appetite.
野心勃勃！只是要記得控制好食量。

q: She ends the book by saying that sharing a meal is the fastest way to understand a culture. In your opinion, which dish best represents your culture?
她在書末說，共享一餐是了解一種文化最快的方式。在你看來，哪道菜最能代表你的文化？
o: Hot pot. It's all about gathering together.
火鍋。重點就是大家聚在一起。
be all about = 重點全在於。gather = 聚集。
A beautiful choice. The shared pot is the culture itself.
很美的選擇。共用的那一鍋本身就是文化。
Beef noodle soup. It carries a lot of history.
牛肉麵。它承載了很多歷史。
carry history = 承載歷史。
Dishes shaped by migration always have the richest stories.
由遷徙塑造的菜總是有最豐富的故事。
A home-cooked family dinner, not one single dish.
一頓家常晚餐，而不是某一道菜。
home-cooked = 家常的、在家煮的。
That may be the wisest answer of all. Culture lives at the family table.
這可能是最有智慧的答案。文化就活在家庭餐桌上。

end: Now I'm planning a slow trip to Taiwan just for the food. Thanks for sharing!
我現在想為了美食規劃一趟台灣慢旅行了。謝謝你的分享！
